Class PixelRef

java.lang.Object
icyllis.arc3d.core.RefCnt
icyllis.arc3d.core.PixelRef
All Implemented Interfaces:
RefCounted
public class PixelRef extends RefCnt
This class is the smart container for pixel memory.
This class may be shared/accessed between multiple threads.

  • Constructor Details

    • PixelRef

      public PixelRef(int width, int height, @Nullable Object base, @NativeType("void *") long address, int rowBytes, @Nullable LongConsumer freeFn)
      Creates PixelRef from width, height. rowBytes should be width times bpp, or larger. freeFn is used to free the address.
      Parameters:
      base - array if heap buffer; may be null
      address - address if native buffer, or array offset; may be NULL
      rowBytes - size of one row of buffer; width times bpp, or larger
      freeFn - free function for native buffer; may be null

  • Method Details

    • makeAllocate

      @SharedPtr public static @Nullable @SharedPtr PixelRef makeAllocate(@NonNull ImageInfo info, int rowBytes)
      Allocate zero-initialized memory for the given image info and row bytes.

      The allocator interface is MemoryUtil.MemoryAllocator. It's typically jemalloc or system allocator, and you can obtain the allocator via MemoryUtil.getAllocator(true).

      Note that while the total allocation size can exceed 2GB, the rowBytes (scanline size in bytes) is restricted to within 2GB. This method may return null if row bytes is invalid for the given image info.

      Parameters:
      info - target image info, must be valid (known color type, alpha type, non-zero dimensions)
      rowBytes - desired row bytes, must be ImageInfo.minRowBytes() or greater, or 0 to use the min row bytes equivalently
      Returns:
      a smart container for allocated pixel memory; null if allocation failed

    • getRowBytes

      public int getRowBytes()
      The size, in bytes, between the start of one pixel row/scanline and the next in buffer, including any unused padding between them. This value must be at least the width multiplied by the bytes-per-pixel, where the bytes-per-pixel depends on the color type.

    • isImmutable

      public boolean isImmutable()
      Returns true if this container is marked as immutable, meaning that the contents of its pixels will not change for the lifetime of the container.

    • setImmutable

      public void setImmutable()
      Marks this container is immutable, meaning that the contents of its pixels will not change for the lifetime of the container. This state can be set on a container, but it cannot be cleared once it is set.
